_about: Everything spoken in the walkthrough. `text` is what the transcript shows; `say` (optional) is what the TTS engine reads. The agent's lines follow build_reference_task() in backend/services/calle_service.py word for word where it prescribes wording (opening, probe, HR-policy response, close).
_voices_note: Kokoro-82M presets, chosen by predicted naturalness (UTMOS22) over 47 candidate voices: af_heart 4.52, am_fenrir 4.50, am_puck 4.50, am_michael 4.39. The Edge voice used in the first video scored 4.35.

narration.text: Reference checks are the part of hiring nobody has time for. Hours of phone tag, for every candidate. RefCheck A.I. hands those calls to Call E.
Every candidate lands on one dashboard, with a score and a clear recommendation.
Question sets are tuned by role, with follow-up probes for vague answers. Each set becomes the result schema Call E fills in on the call.
A new check starts with the candidate and the role.
Then two to four references, and how each one knows the candidate.
And launch. Call E dials every reference at once, each on its own line.
Each call comes back as JSON that Call E has already validated against our schema. The check scores itself, and the recruiter gets an email.
Every reference shows strengths, red flags, quotes, a score for each question, and the full transcript.
Share a read-only link with the hiring manager. Referee contact details stay private.
Hours of phone tag, down to one click. RefCheck A.I., built on Call E.

lines.text: Hello, this is Alex calling from the Northwind recruiting team. Am I speaking with James Okafor?
lines.say: Hello, this is Alex calling from the Northwind recruiting team. Am I speaking with James Okahfor?

lines.text: Great. Maria Chen listed you as a reference, and she's given Northwind permission to contact you. Is now a good time? I'll need about ten minutes.
Oh, sure! Happy to talk about Maria. Go ahead.
To start, how would you describe her technical ability?
Honestly? One of the strongest engineers I've ever managed.
That's helpful. Can you give me a specific example of her best technical work?
Sure. She led our move to a new ledger system, with zero downtime. And she wrote most of the rollback plan herself.
Last question. Would you hire Maria again for an engineering role?
In a heartbeat. If I were starting a team tomorrow, she's the first call I'd make.
Thank you so much for your time. This is genuinely useful to us.

skipped_turns.text: How did you and Maria work together, and for how long?
I was her manager at Tidewater Payments for a little over three years. She was on my payments platform team.
Can you describe a difficult technical problem she solved?
We had a nasty outage on Black Friday. She found the root cause while the rest of us were still triaging.
How would you describe her code quality and engineering practices?
Her code reviews were a masterclass. The whole team got better just by reading them.
How did she work with non-technical teammates?
Really well. Product and support trusted her to explain trade-offs in plain language.
How quickly did she pick up new technologies?
Fast. She was productive on the new ledger stack within a few weeks.
How did she handle tight deadlines or production incidents?
Calm. She's the person you want on the bridge at 2 a.m.
We're considering her for a Senior Software Engineer role that owns our payments platform. How do you think she'd perform?
Very well. That's exactly the work she did for us, and she did it at a senior level.

lines.text: I'm sorry, company policy is that I can only confirm dates and title.
I completely understand, and I appreciate your transparency. Is there anything at all you'd like us to know about Maria as a professional?
Just that she's eligible for rehire. That's all I can share.
lines.say: Just that she's eligible for re-hire. That's all I can share.
